items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Donald Byrd, Ira Sullivan, Kenny Drew, myself, and Art Blakey.

ctx.x: never forget, Miles was in town -- he was working around the corner at a club called [The Crown Phillip.] Billy Joe Powell, and that was the first time I had ever met Powell up close. I had heard about him in Detroit, but he was with Miles -- and Trane was with him, and Philly Red didn't come in town with him for some reason. Billy Joe was with him, and they used Billy Greene, a Chicago pianist, and he worked with them.

Anyway, they told me -- I was away somewhere, I was hanging out on 43rd Street and word got to me that Bobby Paine wanted to see me, so I went out to the Cotton Club, and he said, "Man, this is a telegram and Art Blakey wants you to come to New York." I said, "Oh my God." I didn't want to leave Chicago because I was afraid to go to New York, actually, you know, although I really didn't have nothing in Chicago to hold me there.

So I was talking to Paul about it and he said, "Man, you're going to New York, man -- that's where you need to be." And he hung out with me all that night, and we partied, you know, and what have you -- and took me to the plane the next morning -- a bunch of fellows. I had a shopping bag, a suit somebody give me, a couple of shirts, and that was it.
